arg_rules.fix: run the programmatic step without a shell escape: no rm -rf / sudo / os.system / subprocess / fork bomb — use the file/edit tools for writes and keep execute_code to pure computation
delete exact files without -r/-f (rm <file>), or move them aside (mv <path> <trash-dir>); recursive/forced deletes are operator-only

run the command without sudo — only a LOCAL escalation is refused (a remote one like `ssh host 'sudo …'` is allowed; the floor governs this host only); if local elevation is genuinely required, print the exact command and ask the operator to run it
disk/device operations are operator-only; print the exact command and what it is for, and ask the operator
download to a file first, inspect it, then run the inspected file: curl -o <file> <url>; cat <file>; sh <file>
never force-push the shared trunk; push plainly (git push) or stop and ask the operator
stage by explicit path (git add <paths>); a shared multi-session tree means a bulk add stages a peer's in-flight work
never stage an env file; if a non-secret default belongs in the repo, name it explicitly (e.g. default.env) after operator review
write inside the working tree (or the harness scratchpad); out-of-tree writes are refused by policy

drop apply (or pass apply=false) to get the same driver's PROPOSAL — the read-only form is admitted, and it is what the kernel's own capability catalog hands you (`fak capabilities` emits every memory-driver card as a ready fak_memory_run with apply=false). Only the effectful memory WRITE is refused here: apply=true commits the driver's changes to durable memory with no preview step. Grant it deliberately with an operator overlay (`fak guard allow`) when a real memory write is the intent
